findings.rationale: Observed outcome prevalence (0.433) is far above what the global model predicts from the client's features (mean predicted 0.213), giving calibration-in-the-large of -0.22 (z = -15.1) and ECE z = +12.2, while local AUC (0.808) is normal, so discrimination is intact and only the label prevalence is off. The offset is present from round 1 (CITL negative in almost every round) and is not driven by feature drift. Subgroup O/E is about 2.0-2.3 in both sexes, consistent with a global prevalence offset rather than subgroup-specific under-diagnosis. Its update norm is also anomalous (median norm ratio 4.72) with negative mean cosine, which is what training on shifted labels would produce.

Observed prevalence (0.374) is well above the model's mean prediction (0.167), giving CITL -0.207 (z = -13.9) and ECE z = +9.8, while local AUC (0.843) is normal. The negative CITL appears from round 1 onward, and feature shifts are small and unflagged, so this is a label/prevalence mismatch rather than feature drift. Subgroup O/E is about 2.1-2.3 across both sexes. Update norms are inflated (median norm ratio 3.70) with negative mean cosine, consistent with training on shifted labels.

Observed prevalence (0.305) exceeds the predicted mean (0.143), giving CITL -0.162 (z = -9.8) and ECE z = +6.1 at round 20, with local AUC (0.812) normal. Subgroup O/E is about 1.8-2.1 in both sexes. Update statistics are also anomalous (mean cosine z = -4.4, norm ratio z = +4.1). Confidence is lower than for CA and SC because VT is small (n=324) and its per-round CITL in the drift table is noisy and not consistently negative.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients on updates, local performance, drift, feature tails, and subgroup outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income). Three clients stand out consistently: SC, CA and VT. Each has an observed outcome prevalence far above what its features imply (CITL between -0.16 and -0.22, z-scores of -9.8 to -15.1), while local AUC is normal. That pattern points to prevalence_shift rather than label_noise, which would lower AUC. The offset is present from round 1, and feature drift is absent. Their update norms are also anomalous, which is consistent with training on shifted labels rather than poisoning, since their local data and performance are themselves abnormal. No drift, missing-artefact, subgroup-specific bias, explanation-instability or free-rider signals survived noise adjustment; the remaining feature-tail and subgroup outliers are from small clients with |z_noise| around 3-5 and were not reported. The budget is fully spent (0.0 left). VT is the least certain of the three.
